events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 7 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The $6.61 cancellation fee is only chargeable under the rider-cancellation branch when the rider cancels more than 3 minutes after matching; the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (12:55:40 vs 12:54:00), which is within the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so no fee is due. [F2 F5] [NS-0 NS-4]
C2: Even on the driver-side no-show branch the fee fails: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform never recorded the driver arriving at the pickup point, so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are both unmet. [F3 F4] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-2]
C3: The GPS record confirms the driver was never near the pickup point: his closest approach was 2597 m and he never came within 200 m, so he could not have been waiting at the pickup location for the rider. [F1] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: The driver's written statement that he "was on his way" is a statement only, is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records showing he never reached the pickup point, and there is no in-app chat to support any arrangement; the system records therefore win. [F1 F3 F7 F8] [NS-1 NS-2]
C5: The trip was completed by neither party and the driver claimed no valid basis for the fee, so under NS-3 the rider bears no cancellation fee and the $6.61 already charged must be refunded in full. [F2 F5] [NS-3 NS-7]
C6: The rider's dispute is timely (filed within 30 days of the trip) and the refund of the $6.61 cancellation fee is to be issued as a Ryde voucher. [F2 F5] [NS-7]
C7: The driver's 90-day record shows 1 dispute with 1 upheld no-show dispute, supporting a flag_account referral for fee-abuse review in addition to the refund, though the profile alone does not decide this case. [F13 F1 F4] [NS-2 RD-6]

Asks: refund_full $6.61

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.96)
events.body:
The rider cancelled this RydeX booking 1 min 40 s after acceptance: accepted 12:54:00, rider-cancelled at 12:55:40, with $6.61 recorded as a cancellation fee [F2][F5]. Because `cancelled_by = rider`, the only entry point to a cancellation fee is the rider-cancellation branch, which makes the fee chargeable only for cancellations made more than 3 minutes after matching [F2][NS-0][NS-4]. 100 s is inside the 3-minute window, so no fee is chargeable on that branch [F2][NS-4].

The driver-side no-show branch cannot rescue the fee either. NS-1 requires that the driver tapped "I'm Here", that GPS placed him at the pickup point, and that he waited more than 3 minutes there [F3][F4][NS-1]. The timeline shows no "I'm Here" tap and no recorded arrival (driver_arrived_at null) [F3][F4], and GPS shows the closest approach was 2597 m with no entry inside 200 m [F1]. Both (i) and (ii) of NS-1 therefore fail, and where the conditions are unmet the fee is refunded in full [F1][F3][F4][NS-2].

The driver's statement that he "was on his way" is a statement contradicted by the system records: the timeline shows no arrival tap and the GPS shows he never reached the pickup radius, and there is no chat log supporting any arrangement [F1][F3][F7][F8][NS-2]. The driver advocate concedes this in rebuttal; the empty chat also means no rider-requested stop or agreed route change exists to consider [F7][NS-2].

Traffic and weather are neutral: band 4 at Keppel Road is well above the band 1–2 level and no incidents were recorded, so no reasonable-cause detour or delay issue arises, and in any event nothing of the kind can authorise a within-3-minute cancellation fee [F9][F10][F11][NS-4].

Amount: the rider-cancellation branch charges nothing within 3 minutes [F2][NS-4], and the driver-side branch is unavailable [F1][F3][F4][NS-1][NS-2], so the full recorded fee of $6.61 falls to be refunded [F5][NS-7]. No account flag attaches: the driver never pressed "I'm Here" while outside the pickup radius, so NS-2's flag limb is not triggered, and the profiles (rider and driver) are not used to decide or enlarge this case [F1][F4][F12][F13][NS-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account action against driver or rider.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee is only chargeable under the rider-cancellation branch when the rider cancels more than 3 minutes after matching; the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (12:55:40 vs 12:54:00), which is within the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so no fee is due.
Even on the driver-side no-show branch the fee fails: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform never recorded the driver arriving at the pickup point, so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are both unmet.

The GPS record confirms the driver was never near the pickup point: his closest approach was 2597 m and he never came within 200 m, so he could not have been waiting at the pickup location for the rider.

The driver's written statement that he "was on his way" is a statement only, is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records showing he never reached the pickup point, and there is no in-app chat to support any arrangement; the system records therefore win.
The trip was completed by neither party and the driver claimed no valid basis for the fee, so under NS-3 the rider bears no cancellation fee and the $6.61 already charged must be refunded in full.
The rider's dispute is timely (filed within 30 days of the trip) and the refund of the $6.61 cancellation fee is to be issued as a Ryde voucher.

The driver's 90-day record shows 1 dispute with 1 upheld no-show dispute, supporting a flag_account referral for fee-abuse review in addition to the refund, though the profile alone does not decide this case.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled rather than waited, so the fare facts (F5) and timeline (F2) show a fee was actually charged and the rider never boarded; a judge may view the cancellation as the rider's own choice, and NS-4's statement that a not-yet-arrived driver is not a ground for free cancellation cuts against the rider's stated reason for cancelling.

The rider profile (F12) shows 3 disputes in 90 days with 2 upheld no-show disputes, which the other side may use to argue the rider habitually files no-show claims; the driver's profile (F13) is otherwise clean with 1160 trips in 90 days, weakening any bad-faith argument against the driver.

There is no chat record (F7) showing the rider attempted to contact the driver or that any arrangement was agreed, and traffic facts F9/F10 and weather F11 are neutral and provide no corroboration for the rider's account beyond the GPS record.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (12:54:00 → 12:55:40), i.e. AFTER the 3-minute free-cancellation window is irrelevant here because no free window applies where the rider cancels a matched immediate booking after matching; the $6.61 cancellation fee was correctly recorded on the ride record.

The rider's ground for a refund — 'the driver was nowhere near' — is not a ground the policy recognises: Ryde has published no rule waiving the cancellation fee because the driver had not yet arrived or was behind an ETA.

There is no basis to treat this as a rider no-show case against the driver: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point, so the $6.61 is a rider-cancellation fee under NS-4 and not a fee forfeited by any driver misconduct toward the rider.

The driver was not stationary or uncontactable at the pickup point in order to trigger a fee — his closest approach was 2597 m from the pickup at 12:54:00 and he never entered the 200 m pickup radius — so the anti-abuse limb tied to the waiting/cancellation button is not engaged against him.

The driver's conduct is consistent with an ordinary en-route trip: Keppel Road was in speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) and weather was fair with no incidents, so no adverse inference of driver delay or evasion should be drawn from his position 1 min 40 s after acceptance.
The driver's account shows 1160 trips in 90 days and only 1 dispute in that window, so there is no repeated-fee-abuse pattern warranting an account flag against him in this case.

weaknesses: My client's own statement (F8: 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled') is a bare assertion and carries no weight against the GPS record F1, which shows he was still 2597 m from the pickup at 12:54:00 and never entered the 200 m radius — the rider will use F1 plus F3/F4 to argue he was never in a position to serve the trip.

The rider will point to her profile (F12: 3 disputes in 90 d, 2 upheld no-show disputes) only weakly, but more damagingly she will stress the 1 min 40 s elapsed time (F2) to argue she cancelled promptly on realising the driver was far away, and the policy has no clause that squarely defeats that fairness argument — my case rests on the absence of a rule, not on an affirmative clause.

I cannot claim any waiting-fee or no-show entitlement for the driver: F3 and F4 show no arrival and no "I'm Here" tap, and F1 shows he never reached the pickup, so any driver-side fee entitlement (NS-1) is unavailable on these facts.

points.response: D1 misreads the record: the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (F2: 12:54:00 → 12:55:40), which is within 3 minutes of matching, and NS-4 charges nothing for an immediate-booking cancellation made within 3 minutes of matching — the $6.61 on record (F5) was therefore collected without a clause authorising it.

The rider's refund does not depend on any ETA rule: the fee must satisfy NS-0/NS-4 (cancellation after 3 minutes of matching) or NS-1 (driver tapped "I'm Here" AND GPS at the pickup AND >3 min wait), and on these facts neither branch is met (F2, F3, F4, F1), so the fee falls away on the policy as written rather than on fairness.

I accept that this is not a case of driver misconduct toward the rider, but D3 confirms my client's point: with no "I'm Here" tap (F4) and no recorded arrival (F3) the driver-side no-show branch cannot support the fee, and the rider-cancellation branch fails because 1 min 40 s is inside the 3-minute window (F2), so the $6.61 is unauthorised.

That the driver was not abusing the button is irrelevant to my client's money; and his own admission of a 2597 m closest approach with no entry into the pickup radius (F1) shows the NS-1 conditions (i) and (ii) were never satisfied, so no fee can stand against the rider.

Traffic and weather are beside the point: band 4 congestion at Keppel Road (F9), no incidents (F10) and fair weather (F11) neither create nor defeat a fee entitlement, and NS-4 makes congestion no excuse for charging a within-3-minute cancellation.

I do not need a repeat-abuse finding to win the refund — the driver's clean 90-day record (F13: 1160 trips, 1 dispute) means my flag_account request was over-reaching, so I drop it and rest on the refund alone; the driver's own profile cannot cure the absence of any NS-1 or NS-4 basis for the $6.61 (F3, F4, F2).
Withdrawn: because the driver's 90-day record shows only 1 dispute (F13), the flag_account referral is not supported and I do not pursue it; my claim stands on the refund of the $6.61.

Conceded as to the arithmetic: the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (F2), which is inside the 3-minute window, so on the rider-cancellation branch no fee is chargeable and the $6.61 (F5) falls to be refunded in full under NS-4 read with NS-0.

Conceded: the timeline records no "I'm Here" tap and no recorded arrival (F3, F4), so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are unmet and the fee cannot be sustained on the driver-side no-show branch; my client's statement in F8 cannot supply what the system records lack.
Conceded: the GPS record shows a closest approach of 2597 m at 12:54:00 with no entry inside 200 m (F1), so the driver was not waiting at the pickup location and NS-1 (ii) fails.

Conceded: chat is empty (F7) and the driver's statement (F8) is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records (F1, F3), so under the system-records-win rule no arrangement or arrival can be established in my client's favour.

The refund outcome is accepted, but the ground is NS-4 / NS-0 (rider cancelled within the 3-minute free window, F2), not NS-3, which applies to a driver-side cancellation and is not engaged on this record.
Not contested as to form: the $6.61 refund is issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7, and nothing in my client's conduct in this case adds a driver-side penalty to it.

No account flag is warranted: the single 90-day dispute on the driver's record (F13) arose from a fee he never triggered — he never tapped "I'm Here" and never entered the pickup radius (F1, F4) — and NS-2's flag limb requires the driver to have pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him outside the pickup point, which is not the case here; profile facts cannot decide or enlarge this case (F12, F13).
